E&E News reports that Democrats appeared set for a commanding victory in Tuesday's midterms, potentially gaining control of Congress and several state governments as of 11 p.m. Eastern time. The party attributes its strong performance partly to voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, with energy prices cited as salient issues in many races. Analysts say flipping Congress would give Democrats leverage to hinder Trump's climate rollbacks, issue subpoenas, and influence must-pass funding bills, while state-level wins could enable new clean-energy legislation. The piece notes results were still being counted and that some outcomes remain uncertain.

visual null
items.title: Democratic midterm gains could reshape U.S. climate policy

items.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor suggested 'quockerwodger', an obscure English word, as a replacement for terms like 'andhbhakts' and 'godi'. He described it as someone controlled by another who acts on their instructions. Sharing the definition on X, he asked if it were an acceptable alternative to older labels. This marks his repeated habit of introducing uncommon words into political discourse.
items.title: Tharoor Proposes New Term for Political Puppets

items.summary: As results came in for the November 3 US midterm elections, observers tracked 57 races involving Indian-American candidates across Congress, state legislatures, governorships and local office. Republican Vivek Ramaswamy lost his Ohio gubernatorial bid despite Donald Trump's endorsement. Democrat Pramila Jayapal won re-election to the House from Washington with 87.47% of votes per the Associated Press. Democrats were projected to take control of the House and lead in the Senate as counting continued. At least three other Indian-American Democrats, including Pia Dandiya (51.85%) and Suhas Subramanyam (60.68%), secured early wins. A tally by the Indo-American News Service counted 57 candidates with independently confirmed heritage among one Senate candidate, 11 House candidates, three statewide offices, 36 state legislative seats and six local positions, while another 15 were excluded for unverifiable origin.
items.title: Indian-American Candidates Win and Lose in US Midterm Races

items.summary: PM Narendra Modi called Sharad Pawar on Wednesday morning and advised him to cut down on travel, rest more, improve his diet, and prioritise health amid the 86-year-old's hospital discharge. Pawar was admitted Monday at Pune's Ruby Hall Clinic after cough and chest pain symptoms, then discharged Wednesday in stable condition per cardiologist Dr Purvez K Grant. Associate Vitthal Maniyar relayed Modi's guidance; Supriya Sule may shoulder duties during rest. A planned November 3 Baramati visit was postponed to a possible November 16 date pending confirmation.
items.title: Modi Advises Rest as NCP Chief Discharged

items.summary: Texas elected its first Democratic senator in nearly four decades and its first Democratic governor since 1990 on Tuesday night. The results drew attention amid a wave of corporate relocations to the state, including SpaceX, Tesla, Chevron, and Caterpillar seeking lower taxes and lighter regulation. Republican nominee Ken Paxton and Gov. Greg Abbott received substantial backing from Elon Musk's campaign funds, which Democrat Gina Hinojosa used as central attack points in her victory over Abbott. The upsets carried outsized national significance given Texas business influence nationwide.
items.title: Democrats Win Texas Senate and Governorship After Decades-Long Droughts

items.summary: US voters in Tuesday's midterms delivered large Democratic gains across Republican strongholds including Texas, South Carolina, Ohio and Kansas. Democrats are projected to take both chambers of Congress, marking a significant reversal for Trump. Exit polls conducted by SSRS for US media organisations found nearly nine in 10 voters cited the cost of living as crucial or major; CNN's poll showed more than six in 10 disapproved of Trump, while AP data indicated around six in 10 believed he prioritised personal interests. Younger and Hispanic voters shifted back toward Democrats. Analysts note limits remain due to Trump's veto powers and a 60-vote Senate threshold.
items.title: Democrats' Midterm Surge Attributed to Economy, War and Trump Fatigue

items.summary: Ram Madhav, BJP's national vice president, said the party has no involvement in the National Conference's internal affairs after Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi resigned. A senior BJP leader speaking anonymously linked the statement to allegations of electoral malpractices and fears of a government-impacting split. The article notes the BJP faces similar accusations over past splits, including those involving Mamata Banerjee and Eknath Shinde.
items.title: BJP Denies Role in NC Fracture Amid MP Resignation

items.summary: A third Energy Community Secretariat report on the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism finds that day-ahead trading across Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo*, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia rose to about 2.97 TWh in Q3, roughly 10% above Q2 but up around 80% versus a year earlier per one exchange's data. This growth coincided with lower scheduled exchanges between the six Western Balkan parties and EU neighbours, so the secretariat noted it cannot be attributed solely to CBAM and that the available data do not show its cause.
items.title: Western Balkan Power Exchanges See Q3 Volume Rise Amid Lower EU Trade

items.summary: Reflecting on his party's midterm losses, US President Donald Trump suggested voters support his Iran posture but resisted higher gasoline prices tied to the war. He called price pressure a short-term problem for long-term gain and said Americans could "finish the job" if Tehran fails to cooperate. The remarks followed Democratic gains in Congress projected by US media.
items.title: Trump Ties Midterm Losses to Gas Prices Amid Iran War Debate

items.summary: Democrats took control of the Senate, ending a Republican majority that had entered the midterms as an apparent red wall. The GOP lost seats across Maine, Ohio, Texas, Kansas, Iowa, South Carolina and North Carolina while failing to flip New Hampshire and Georgia. Democrats credited strong candidate quality and campaign spending for their gains, with Ossoff raising over $100 million and Cooper over $49 million through mid-October.
items.title: Democrats Capture Senate Control in Midterm Upset

items.summary: Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra has shifted focus from the concluded INDIA opposition bloc rally against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to preparing the party's machinery ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. She held a closed-door meeting with three senior UP Congress leaders, finalizing names for committees including manifesto, management, campaign and coordination panels, which will be forwarded to president Mallikarjun Kharge after Diwali. A committee overseeing ties with Samajwadi Party (SP) is also being formed, with Priyanka likely involved in seat-sharing talks with Akhilesh Yadav. She is expected to spearhead the UP campaign after Diwali across four regions.
items.title: Priyanka Gandhi Mobilizes Congress for Uttar Pradesh Polls

items.summary: On Wednesday, US President Donald Trump blamed Fox News for Republican losses in the midterm elections, accusing the network of undermining conservative candidates by giving airtime to Democrats. Writing on Truth Social, he said 'Fox News bears responsibility for these losses.' He singled out former New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio, questioning why the network let him offer advice while claiming he left office in disgrace. The remarks came as Democrats were projected to win control of the Senate and secure a House majority.
items.title: Trump Blames Fox News for Republican Midterm Losses

items.summary: Indian-American Republican Vivek Ramaswamy lost the Ohio governor's race to Democrat Amy Acton, according to US media. As of 8:40 am IST, Acton polled 50.4 per cent of the vote while Ramaswamy won 46.3 per cent, per NBC News. If he had prevailed, he would have become Ohio's first Indian-American governor and its second-richest governor, Forbes reported. Trump endorsed Ramaswamy but called Acton a Radical Left Democrat. Acton becomes the state's first woman governor in two decades; she lacks elective experience amid unprecedented $100 million spent against her.
items.title: Amy Acton Defeats Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio Governor's Race

items.summary: Crude oil prices rebounded earlier in the day after falling to their lowest level in four weeks, as traders turned attention from U.S. midterms to developments in the Middle East war. At the time of writing, Brent crude traded at $103.60 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate at $95.98 per barrel. Energy consultancies cautioned against excessive optimism over Gulf supply recovery.
items.title: Oil Prices Rebound on Middle East Supply Fears

items.summary: US President Donald Trump said Washington has no immediate plans to strike Iran, even as The New York Times reported a US Central Command plan could launch an attack by the following day. In interviews with The Financial Times and Fox & Friends, Trump described the situation as contented, saying they are 'locked and loaded' but there may be no reason for action. He also confirmed strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said his country is ready for battle; President Masoud Pezeshkian urged dialogue.
items.title: Trump denies immediate plans for strike on Iran amid reports of imminent attack

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government permitted public firecracker bursting only between 6 am–7 am and 7 pm–8 pm during Deepavali, aiming to curb air and noise pollution. Officials urged residents toward environment-friendly practices over high-decibel fireworks. The move follows the 2018 Supreme Court judgment restricting sales to reduced-emission green crackers, with the TNPCB running awareness campaigns across schools and institutions.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Limits Firecrackers to Two Hours on Deepavali

items.summary: Two gold traders travelling from Coimbatore to supply jewellery shops were robbed near the railway station in Ongole in the early hours of Wednesday. Unidentified miscreants waylaid them, allegedly assaulted and threatened them, then fled with about 2 kg of gold. Based on a complaint lodged by the victims, Ongole II Town police registered a case and launched an investigation.
items.title: Two Gold Traders Robbed of 2 kg in Ongole

items.summary: A Poundland supplier, Highcrest Retail Brands, says it could lose a few million pounds if the retailer enters administration. Adam Turner, sales director at the family-owned Bradford business with about £50m turnover, told the BBC that Poundland is one of its biggest customers after decades of trading. He said other small and medium-sized suppliers face similar risk. This follows founder Steve Smith's warning that two or three thousand single-brand suppliers would be affected. Around 12,000 staff could lose jobs, with roughly 6,000 not re-employed if stores are only partly sold. Business secretary Jonathan Reynolds met Gordon Brothers after questioning why a solvent deal had not been made.
items.title: Poundland supplier warns of millions in losses amid collapse fears

items.summary: The BJP is holding marches and rallies across Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi under its 'Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy' campaign. Union Health Minister J P Nadda will march in Bhopal on Wednesday, while national president Nitin Nabin leads a Gorakhpur rally at 12 noon alongside Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The party frames the events as opposition attempts to destabilise democratic processes ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.
items.title: BJP Holds Save Democracy Rallies Ahead of Uttar Pradesh Elections

items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate searched 11 premises in Kerala and Tamil Nadu on Wednesday under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, officials said. The probe concerns R Premkumar, founding member and de facto Chairman and Managing Director of the Bharath Lajhna Multi State Co-operative Society (BLM). It is alleged he diverted public deposits to his wife and relatives, pledged the Society's Ragam Theatre without funds reaching it, and acquired about 500 acres at Kanchipuram in his wife's name. The Kochi office conducted the searches.
items.title: ED raids Kerala and Tamil Nadu over money laundering probe

items.summary: Democratic candidate Gina Hinojosa defeated incumbent Republican Greg Abbott in Texas's gubernatorial election, becoming the state's first Democratic governor since 1990. Her campaign centered on halting new data center development pending stronger resident protections and subsidies reform. As Texas hosts roughly a quarter of planned U.S. AI capacity with projected investment rising from $3.4 billion to over $66 billion by 2026, her proposed moratorium could disrupt billions in infrastructure projects.
items.title: Texas Democrat Governor Emerges Amid AI Data Center Boom Uncertainty

items.summary: Geoffrey Hinton, described as one of the “godfathers of AI”, told the Guardian that humanity might have been better off never developing the technology. He warned it could trigger a large-scale incident this year or next — such as an electricity brownout or a week-long collapse of financial systems — and said either later this year or next year people would see something like Chornobyl, which “may be enough to make people really pay attention.” Hinton is not calling himself a doomer; he believes AI could bring a wonderful future but insists the risks must be managed. He criticized leaders at OpenAI, whose chief executive Sam Altman he does not trust “at all”, and backed mandatory testing of frontier models, endorsed by Finland and 32 other countries.
items.title: AI godfather Geoffrey Hinton warns humans may have been better off without AI

items.summary: The new iPad Mini keeps its small form but swaps the LCD for an OLED display previously reserved for the iPad Pro. It costs $100 more than the prior model, which had itself risen $100 in June amid RAM shortages, bringing the entry price to $699—a 40% jump and just $50 below the cheapest iPad Air. Apple also cut thickness by 16%, weight by 13.8% for Wi-Fi models, and shrank the display border 25% to grow the screen from 8.3 to 8.5 inches.
items.title: Apple's New iPad Mini Brings OLED and a Price Hike

items.summary: FARMZER0 founder Russell Steinberg is turning empty downtown Chicago office space into vertical farms that grow edible greens for local restaurants and residents. The company requires only vacant space, which he estimates at about 45 million square feet in the city. A single site uses roughly 650 square feet to feed nearby buildings.
items.title: Chicago Startup Converts Vacant Office Space Into Vertical Farms

items.summary: Alphabet's Google announced a US$15 billion investment in Malaysia spanning 2027 to 2028, directed toward data centre campuses, clean energy, water security and worker upskilling. The spending will fund new campuses in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan alongside its operational Elmina Business Park site. Google projects the construction phase could add an annual average of US$1. 1 billion to Malaysia's GDP and support more than 37,000 local jobs per year during building, with facilities expected to sustain over 9,000 jobs once running at wages averaging 45% above the national median.
items.title: Google Commits $15 Billion Investment in Malaysia for Data Centres and Clean Energy

items.summary: Alphabet's Google expanded voluntary exit packages in June across Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland as it seeks to curb rising costs amid heavy artificial intelligence spending. A spokesperson said the program supports important work ahead. Reuters could not determine how many employees accepted the latest round. In Switzerland, where Google employs about 5,000 people, at least four in a team of about 50 reportedly left after accepting one month's salary per year of service.
items.title: Google Expands Voluntary Buyout Offers Amid AI Spending

items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview with podcaster Raj Shamani that India has become OpenAI's largest market by ChatGPT users, surpassing the United States. He attributed this to strong enthusiasm for AI among Indian users and cited a student who used the tools to run school fundraising without prior experience. Altman also noted Americans appear unusually negative toward AI on expressed preference.
items.title: OpenAI's Altman Calls India Its Largest ChatGPT Market, Surpassing the US

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India constituted a Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets headed by Deputy Governor Rohit Jain, comprising eight external members. The committee will meet at least quarterly and examine issues across money, government securities, foreign exchange and derivative markets, plus trading, clearing and settlement infrastructure.
items.title: RBI Forms Technical Panel for Financial Markets Under Rohit Jain

items.summary: Bloomberg Economics reports RBI's foreign exchange reserves may dip below $500 billion in October after reducing forward liabilities. Rising crude oil prices, foreign investment outflows of about $30 billion, and US trade policy uncertainty weigh on the rupee. Relief could come from lower oil prices or a trade deal.
items.title: RBI's Forex Reserves Fall Below $500 Billion Amid Rupee Pressure

items.summary: At the launch of The Library, a new cultural space at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre in Mumbai on 31 October 2026, Nita Ambani wore Wallace Chan's 'Soaring Spirit' dragonfly brooch. The piece reportedly took about a decade to create and incorporates a 17.67-carat tsavorite garnet with diamonds, ruby, pink sapphire and titanium. Its estimated market value ranges from $1.5 million to $1.8 million, or approximately ₹12 crore to ₹15 crore. The brooch is dated 2017 and draws on the dragonfly's symbolism of freedom and harmony with nature. Ambani paired it with a beige linen pantsuit; the appearance came just before her 63rd birthday.
items.title: Nita Ambani Wears ₹15 Crore Dragonfly Brooch at The Library Launch

items.summary: Tesla registered 990 cars in India from January to October 2026, per Vahan data via TradingView, reaching about 1,217 since launch. A ₹9 lakh cut on the Model Y Premium RWD drove most of this year's sales: 38 in June rose to a record 291 in September. Tesla led luxury EVs with a 30% share but held just 0.8% of India's electric passenger market, as Tata registered 14,669 cars in October alone.
items.title: Tesla India sales surge after Model Y price cut

items.summary: Apple released developer beta versions of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3, adding always-listening artificial intelligence tools to Series 12 and Ultra 4 smartwatches that were unveiled at a September event. The features include Siri Recap and Live Rewind for transcribing conversations, available only in English during testing. A full rollout is scheduled for December.
items.title: Apple Releases Beta Versions of AI Listening Tools and Health App

items.summary: Former OpenAI employees, cited by five people familiar with the matter, said they had warned leadership and the board for years about lax security practices before ChatGPT launched in late 2022. They argued that storing most code in a single repository let anyone accessing it see details of sensitive projects, and that management seemed more focused on matching competitors like Google and Anthropic than protecting information from foreign governments. The disclosures follow an October arrest of engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan for planting a hidden recording device. OpenAI said the warnings reflect broader tensions as AI becomes a national asset while slowing security can delay progress and complicate planned IPOs. A spokesperson, Elana Widmann, called OpenAI one of the most targeted organizations in the world and pointed to recent internal sprints under chief information security officer Dane Stuckey as evidence its defenses are improving.
items.title: OpenAI Workers Flagged Long-Standing Security Weaknesses Before ChatGPT

items.summary: Apple expanded its warnings in a recent annual filing, cautioning that autonomous AI agents could access systems without authorization, send communications and complete transactions unpredictably. The disclosure follows similar concerns from Alphabet and Microsoft, amid industry incidents including an OpenAI attack on Hugging Face this summer. Apple's CEO John Ternus stressed user awareness of granted permissions as the company develops AI features.
items.title: Apple Warns AI Agents May Threaten Systems

items.summary: Cryptocurrencies briefly dipped on Nov 4 as Democrats won majorities in the US Senate and House, a potential blow to an industry seeking faster deregulation. Bitcoin touched a six-week low before recovering near US$78,070. The market has lost some US$300 billion since October's record above US$122,000, while a US$6 billion Binance hack—the largest heist in history—further weighed on sentiment. Tim Sun of HashKey said the market may be re-evaluating crypto's risk-reward profile amid security and legislative headwinds.
items.title: Crypto Dips After Democrat Midterm Wins and Binance Hack

items.summary: The US Democratic Party won control of both houses of Congress in the midterms, picking up 53 Senate seats and 222 House seats as at 3pm on Nov 4 Singapore time. Analysts at BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, said Trump would likely face legislative resistance but could continue through executive orders, while warning that slower data-centre construction and AI investment could weigh on the US economy. In Asia, stocks dipped then recovered after the result; Singapore’s Straits Times Index fell 76 points in the morning to 5,256.93 at midday. DBS Group Research strategist Philip Wee noted market-implied odds of a December rate hike had fallen to 73.5% from 90.8%, and flagged November as an opportunity for Singapore investors amid potential weakness.
items.title: Asian investors weigh Democratic midterm sweep for markets

items.summary: India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In has gained access to Anthropic's Mythos AI model and will begin using it cautiously to assess how best to leverage its capabilities in identifying cyber vulnerabilities, IT Ministry sources said on Tuesday. The approach emphasizes caution as the process unfolds slowly over time.
items.title: CERT-In Gains Access To Anthropic's Mythos AI Model For Cybersecurity Testing

items.summary: Google is switching its school tools from default-on to opt-in, meaning K-12 students lose Google Search unless administrators enable it alongside Gemini features. The change reverses an August 2025 outcry over automatic activation and follows consultations with educators. Chris Phillips called for schools to control classroom AI. Reports place rollout in early 2027; the pilot of Guided Learning arrives this month.
items.title: Google Ties School Search Access To AI Opt-In

items.summary: Published Nov 4, 2026, the article argues that dire predictions of imminent artificial general intelligence are unfounded while AI’s energy use poses a real climate threat. The authors call estimates of an AGI apocalypse probability baseless, noting no one can specify how to achieve AGI and citing evidence against rapid “intelligence explosion” claims by Alan Chan, Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio. They dismiss reports that OpenAI models went rogue as anthropomorphic misreadings of reward hacking. The credible risk is climate: AI energy demand could reach 3 percent of global consumption by 2030, with most met by fossil fuels. A United Nations report says warming may exceed the 1.5 degree Paris target and reach 2.8 degrees by century’s end, requiring an 18 percent emissions cut before decade’s end to avoid catastrophe.
items.title: Authors Reject Imminent AGI Doom and Stress Climate Risk

items.summary: Ahead of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China Southern Power Grid expert Liang Lingyu outlines a shift toward an AI‑native power grid. He frames accelerating green‑energy transition as urgent amid climate pressures and surging demand from the artificial‑intelligence boom, calling coordinated development of six key infrastructure networks — water, electricity, computing, communications, urban underground utilities and logistics — central to building safe, reliable and affordable systems. China's framework rests on four AI‑native pillars: interaction, architecture, processes and tool integration, applied through platforms such as E‑Hong, Da‑Wate and Tian‑Quan; one task that once took days now completes in 10 minutes. He proposes APEC cooperation across joint R&D, cross‑border pilots, standards alignment and infrastructure collaboration to advance green energy and AI integration.
items.title: China Southern Power Grid pitches AI‑native grid at APEC

items.summary: China released two flagship internet reports, the China Internet Development Report 2026 and World Internet Development Report 2026, published by the China Academy of Cyberspace Studies (CACS) on Wednesday. A CACS representative said improving digital inclusion is central to China's digital society drive. By end of 2025, rural broadband users reached 204 million as AI literacy and accessibility efforts expanded nationwide.
items.title: China Releases Two Internet Development Reports at Wuzhen Summit

items.summary: An analysis by Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) says the Democrats’ midterm loss is unlikely to change President Donald Trump’s trade course, since both parties now favor economic nationalism and strong supply chains. GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava expects heightened pressure on India for a fast agreement that opens its market to American goods while securing concessions for US businesses. He warns New Delhi should demand reciprocal concessions under WTO rules rather than accept what he calls economic coercion.
items.title: GTRI Warns Trump May Coerce India Into Quick Trade Deal

items.summary: BLS Polymers Ltd.'s shares rose about 6% on their first trading day, opening at Rs 244 on the BSE and Rs 248 on the NSE against an issue price of Rs 150 per share. The book-built listing attracted strong demand: overall subscription reached 241.22 times, with non-institutional investors subscribing 559.20 times, qualified institutional buyers 200.25 times and retail individual investors 128.36 times. BLS Polymers manufactures polymer compounds for wires, cables and pipelines, serving more than 190 customers across six countries. Total income rose 5% to Rs 354 crore in FY26 from Rs 337 crore, while profit after tax climbed 28% to Rs 27 crore from Rs 21 crore. Proceeds will fund capital expenditure and working capital of about Rs 167 crore. The article was written by Surbhi Khanna, who is not a SEBI-registered research analyst or investment advisor.
items.title: BLS Polymers Shares Jump After Strong IPO Debut

items.summary: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Wednesday rejected Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's challenge for a public debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, saying the discussion should happen in Parliament rather than on the streets. In posts and video shared on X, Sarma mocked Gandhi over his Diwali greeting while holding a rose, writing that roses are given on Valentine's Day, not Diwali. He urged Gandhi to fulfil his duties as Leader of the Opposition and said issues such as Bofors and the Bhopal Gas Tragedy could be debated there without disruption. Earlier, Rahul had challenged Modi 24 hours prior, proposing a table-based debate with media and youth present.
items.title: Assam CM Sarma Rejects Gandhi's Street Debate Challenge

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi called NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar on Wednesday after the 85-year-old was discharged from a private hospital in Pune. A close associate, Vitthal Maniyar, said Modi spoke with warmth and suggested complete rest while Supriya would look after the country. Pawar thanked Modi and assured he would recover.
items.title: Modi Advises Pawar Complete Rest After Discharge

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang delivered a keynote speech on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at the opening ceremony of the 2026 World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province. The event was held in Wuzhen, and Xinhua reported that the full text translation is available as an attachment.
items.title: Li Qiang Delivers Keynote at WIC Wuzhen Summit Opening

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Commerce Minister Wang Wentao co-chaired the 37th APEC Ministerial Meeting by video conference in Beijing on November 3, 2026. Wang Yi said China is ready to work with all parties during the final stage of the 2026 APEC 'China Year.' The leaders' meeting will be hosted in Shenzhen from November 18-19, marking China's third hosting after Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. Wang Yi noted more than 300 meetings have been held during the China Year.
items.title: China Co-Chairs APEC Ministerial Meeting Ahead of Shenzhen Leaders' Summit

items.summary: After Democrats took control of Congress in the 2026 midterms, European shares rose with banks and clean energy stocks leading gains while defence fell. Gold jumped to $4,046 an ounce as investors reassessed Trump-era policy risks on AI regulation and taxes.
items.title: European markets rise as Democrats win US midterms

items.summary: Brussels is quietly preparing to take the lead on discussions about the next round of support for Ukraine, according to a live blog by Jakub Krupa. The European Commission will hold talks with the US, France, Germany, Britain, Nato, and the World Bank on helping Kyiv through winter and supporting the peace process ahead of negotiations in Abu Dhabi.
items.title: EU to lead Ukraine support talks with US and partners

items.summary: More than 100 US expats and election enthusiasts gathered in a Surry Hills pub to watch the American midterms, celebrating after news of the Democrats' historic Senate win. Katrena Henderson said she had not been this excited about an election in a long time, while Associate Professor David Smith called it "a referendum on Trump." Cindy Herman-Jones mailed in her ballot for Senator James Talarico's seat flip despite never voting abroad before. First-time voter Aliana Hensel watched closely after missing the presidential election. Meanwhile, Republican watchers at another Sydney pub observed how Americans respond to their political situation.
items.title: US expats celebrate Democratic midterm win at Sydney watch parties

items.summary: Based on projected results, Democrats have won both the US Senate and House of Representatives, taking control of Congress for the remainder of Donald Trump's presidency. The article lists several historic firsts: Hakeem Jeffries is poised to become speaker; Abdul El-Sayed becomes the first Muslim senator after defeating Mike Rogers in Michigan; Texas turns blue with James Talarico winning a Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa becoming its first Latina governor; Keisha Lance Bottoms wins Georgia as its first black female governor, while Chris Pappas becomes the first openly gay man elected to the Senate. Trump conceded that Democrats did a 'good job' but reserved his presidential veto power over Texas legislation. The BBC reported scenes of celebration and sombre concession across several states. Representative Chris Pappas had served in the House since 2019 before running for the Senate, which he lost by four years to two decades without a Democratic governor in Georgia's history.
items.title: Democrats Capture Both Chambers in Midterm Firsts

items.summary: Liverpool owner Fenway Sports Group has held talks about buying a majority stake in the Cadillac Formula One team for more than £2bn, as Mark Walter continues selling sporting assets amid insurance-fraud allegations. TWG Global denies fraud and says no sale is imminent; Walter values his share at about £2.24bn. FSG declined to comment on its plans.
items.title: FSG in Talks for Majority Stake in Cadillac F1 Team

items.summary: Delhi's air quality index crossed 300, entering the 'very poor' category and prompting authorities to invoke Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan. The plan introduces heavier road cleaning, higher parking charges and more public transport, while Delhi Metro added 20 weekday train trips. Officials said the measures followed forecasts predicting continued very poor air over coming days. A recent storm had cleared pollution before northwesterly winds returned to carry smoke from crop-residue burning in Punjab and Haryana. With Diwali approaching, concerns remain that fireworks could worsen conditions further. India's Supreme Court permitted certified green firecrackers only during limited windows on 7 and 8 November, while banning them within 300m of hospitals, schools and care homes. Enforcing the rules remains a challenge as conventional crackers continue to be sold despite bans.
items.title: Delhi invokes pollution curbs as air turns very poor before Diwali

items.summary: A DW article explains that the outcome of the US midterm election will shape policy for years with global repercussions. Democrats secured majorities in both chambers of Congress after Tuesday's vote, which could shift foreign policy issues including support for Ukraine, a possible end to the war against Iran launched on February 28, 2026, and funding for development aid projects cut back by President Trump shortly after his second term began. DW editor Brandon Conradis noted Democrats can push legislation providing more aid to Ukraine. Michael O'Hanlon of Brookings Institution said Congress could perhaps prevent major escalation by refusing to fund it. The article notes there will be no complete reversal, as the US remains a country with a Republican president.
items.title: US Midterm Election Outcomes Shape Foreign Policy in Ukraine, Iran and Aid

items.summary: Talk of Germany joining the Global Combat Air Program (GCAP) with Japan, Britain and Italy gained momentum after German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius expressed interest. During a Monday meeting in Berlin, Pistorius discussed participation with British defense chief Wes Streeting about the trilateral next-generation fighter jet project. However, Japanese concerns about further delays to negotiations remain.
items.title: Germany's interest in GCAP fighter program grows amid Japanese concerns

items.summary: DTE Electric of southeast Michigan has filed a long-range integrated resource plan with the state public service commission proposing two new gas-fired power plants totaling 2.1 GW, online in 2031 and 2032, relying on carbon capture and sequestration to comply with law requiring zero-carbon generation by 2040. Critics argue CCS has not been successfully deployed by U.S. utilities and that public opposition is likely strong. DTE estimates $6.4 billion for the plants, though costs may rise. Advocates see the plan as tied to new data center demand from Oracle and Google rather than merely replacing retiring coal generation. State regulators will study whether to approve it over the coming year.
items.title: Michigan Utility's Carbon Capture Plan Faces Scrutiny Over Gas Investment

items.summary: Two cranberry bogs in southeastern Massachusetts are harvesting berries beneath operating solar panels, marking what may be the first such dual-use setup in the country and possibly the world. The projects sit over a 4.4-megawatt array with a 13.5-megawatt-hour battery in Kingston and a 1-MW array in Plymouth, built by Greenbacker Renewables with Distributed Energy Infrastructure. Prateek Tare called it “literally proving it can be done.” The work addresses Massachusetts’ site-siting challenges as the state pursues net-zero carbon emissions by 2050, using agrivoltaics to keep productive wetland bogs in use while generating power above them.
items.title: First Cranberry Bogs in the U.S. Grow Under Working Solar Panels

items.summary: The minister in charge of foreign-national policy says Japan is unlikely to expand the cap for its Specified Skilled Workers Type I visa category, which targets labor-short industries like food service. Business groups are asking the government to reconsider restrictions after applications were halted in April when the industry was projected to reach a maximum 50,000 workers. However, last month the government said it plans adjustments to accept more foreign workers for meal services at medical and welfare facilities starting next April.
items.title: Japan Keeps Foreign Worker Cap Despite Labor Shortages

items.summary: Xavier Becerra won Tuesday night as the first Latino governor of California in more than 150 years, according to early projections. At 68 and with a career that includes heading Health and Human Services under President Biden, he defeated Republican Steve Hilton just minutes after polls closed. Governor Gavin Newsom congratulated him shortly after the results were released. The race unfolded amid an ongoing legal fight between California officials and the Department of Justice over federal challenges to more than 20,000 voters' citizenship.
items.title: Becerra Becomes California's First Hispanic Governor in Over a Century

items.summary: The Democratic Party achieved a rare midterm upset, gaining control of both chambers of Congress by winning at least four seats each — far more than expected. Democrats seized the South Carolina Senate seat from Darline Graham after Trump’s endorsement failed to sway voters; James Talarico defeated Ken Paxton in Texas with 59.4% against 66.1% counted, raising over $139 million for his campaign. A New York Times investigation into Roger Marshall’s clinic suing about 700 patients and charging 18% late fees proved decisive in Kansas. In Ohio, a Trump-linked ad backfired on Vivek Ramaswamy; Susan Collins conceded defeat in Maine as counts continued.
items.title: Democrats Sweep Key U.S. Races in Midterm Upset

items.summary: Vivek Ramaswamy lost the Ohio governor's race, ending hopes of a third Indian-origin state governor after Bobby Jindal and Nikki Haley. His defeat came amid broader anti-Republican voting as Democrats flipped traditional strongholds. Democrats won 54 Senate seats, flipping seven from Republicans, and secured 225 House seats. US media projected the results while vote counting continued; Trump said he would accept them.
items.title: Ramaswamy Loses Ohio; Democrats Gain Ground in US Midterms

items.summary: Adam Dare of Eco Renewables argues that in homes switching from gas boilers to air-to-water heat pumps under the Boiler Upgrade Scheme, surplus rooftop PV is better used by a heat pump than an immersion diverter. An immersion element converts one kWh of electricity into one kWh of heat; Energy Systems Catapult measured a median seasonal performance factor of 2. 80 across 291 air source heat pumps in the government’s Electrification of Heat trial, so each unit delivers several kWh per kWh drawn. On Ofgem’s October to December 2026 cap of 26. 32 p and Catapult’s median of 2. 80 p, feeding surplus into a heat pump saves up to three times as much as using it for hot water. Dare concedes diverters still handle small or broken-cloud surpluses that a compressor may ignore, so tariff choice should set the controls first.
items.title: Heat pump edges out immersion diverter for UK surplus solar hot water

items.summary: A commentator argues that a recent US election proceeded without threatening democracy or risking fascism, and that critics predicting such outcomes were mistaken. The piece frames the result as vindicating socially moderate Democrats while listing topics—tariffs, war with Iran, wealth taxes, gerrymandering—that it says have lost political favor. It presents these views as opinion rather than reporting verified facts about election results or public sentiment.
items.title: Commentator dismisses claims of American democratic collapse after election

items.summary: Residents of Sandy Bay, Hobart reported thick, dark-orange water gushing from taps on Tuesday following a burst water main on Regent Street. Emma Thornley said the liquid ran gritty and foul-tasting before clearing; another resident, Glen Christensen, found sediment in bathwater meant for his young granddaughter. TasWater initially told residents the water was safe to drink but updated its advice after learning of the discolouration's severity. The utility attributed the issue to sediment settling in pipes after an outage and said crews flushed lines. It restored supply by 5.30pm, citing aging infrastructure as a driver for planned upgrades.
items.title: Tasmanian resident told orange water was safe to drink after main burst

items.summary: As mid-term election votes were counted, Democrats took control of the US Senate and House from Republicans as results emerged Tuesday. By 1.30 pm Wednesday Indian time, AP reported Democrats holding 54 seats to Republicans' 43 in the Senate, with five still uncalled; in the Lower House they won 225 seats against 136 for Republicans, leaving 74 uncalled. Analysts view the shift as a verdict on Trump's second term amid rising living costs and his tariffs.
items.title: Democrats Seize Control of Congress in Midterm Elections

items.summary: Retailer David Jones faces speculation it may enter voluntary administration after falling behind on rent, with its board reportedly weighing the store's future. Consumer Policy Research Centre CEO Erin Turner urged customers to redeem existing gift cards quickly while avoiding new purchases amid uncertainty, warning that in liquidation card holders rank as unsecured creditors and could lose their money entirely. Professor Gary Mortimer of Queensland University of Technology noted administrators might honour cards with conditions or let business continue normally. The ABC reported a recent redemption failure was due to a temporary third-party outage; David Jones did not respond to questions before publication.
items.title: David Jones Faces Administration Fears; Experts Advise Customers on Gift Cards and Purchases

items.summary: The Indian Solar Manufacturers Association (ISMA) report projects that, under a Vision 2047 scenario assuming full implementation of planned programs, India could reach cumulative solar PV manufacturing capacities totalling approximately 3,484 GW for modules by 2047. The pathway would create about 3.23 million jobs and attract roughly $89 billion in investment, while reducing the annual import bill from around $4.4 billion to zero by 2041. ISMA secretary general Amit Manohar described it as an unprecedented opportunity for a globally competitive ecosystem. The report notes that policy certainty, sustained demand and timely implementation are critical, without stating these outcomes as guaranteed.
items.title: ISMA Forecasts India’s Solar Manufacturing Could Reach 3.48 TW by 2047

items.summary: A suspected cyberattack damaged at least four Coop stores—three in Catania and one in Palermo—in Sicily, raising refrigeration temperatures above 50 degrees and forcing shopkeepers to discard spoiled food. The incident mirrors attacks across Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Estonia, Ireland and France on 12 October that pushed fridges past 50°C. Coop Radenza's Danilo Radenza confirmed the attack but said screening found no further damage; police are investigating links with other countries.
items.title: Cyberattack Damages Coop Supermarkets in Sicily Amid Wider European Outage

items.summary: At least six schools in Bhopal closed on Wednesday due to traffic disruptions expected from a Bharatiya Janata Party march demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, per Dainik Bhaskar. The rally protested Opposition protests since October 2 over concerns about the Election Commission's functioning and electoral roll revisions. Congress leaders Jitu Patwari and Abhinav Baroliya criticized children bearing the brunt and questioned education becoming hostage to political programs during Dhanteras. A district education officer had ordered schools to assess traffic impact before deciding on holidays, The Times of India reported.
items.title: Bhopal Schools Close Ahead of BJP March Over Election Commission Protests

items.summary: As EU countries negotiate funding for their next long-term budget covering 2028–2034, cancer organisations fear that merging health financing with biotechnology, agriculture and the bioeconomy under a broader European Competitiveness Fund could discontinue ongoing projects. Cancer groups warn this risks losing backing for initiatives spanning prevention to patient support. A Commission spokesperson said EU4Health measures would generally remain eligible for competitive funding. Countries have adopted a partial negotiating position, though final allocations are still being discussed ahead of an expected year-end agreement. The Parliament's public health committee requested at least €10.05 billion for health and €2.5 billion for cancer action; the European Cancer Organisation called for €10 billion in health funding including €2 billion for a dedicated cancer fund, protected from industrial competition.
items.title: EU Cancer Groups Warn of Funding Squeeze Under Next Long-Term Budget

items.summary: In November's midterm elections, Democrats captured both chambers of the US Congress and several governorships, marking a broad rejection of President Donald Trump. Exit polls conducted by SSRS for a consortium including major networks and the Associated Press found nearly 9 in 10 voters rated cost of living as crucial or major; many said they felt worse off than two years ago. Democrats gained ground through strong turnout among party faithful and independents, aided by fielding candidates in every race. Trump conceded but deflected blame to gasoline prices and Iran, citing his veto power. Hakeem Jeffries is positioned to become the first Black House Speaker as new majorities are sworn in January 2026.
items.title: Democrats Win Midterm Landslide, Defeat Trump in Congress

items.summary: Donald Trump’s Republican Party took a stunning rebuke in the US midterm elections, facing what looked like its worst defeat in 50 years. Republicans hoped polls might be wrong and that they could at least hold the Senate, but by midnight in Washington the GOP faced losses across swing districts, deep-red states such as Texas and South Carolina, gerrymandered seats and even ones analysts called safe. Voters appear fed up with high prices, the war in Iran and what is being described as Trump administration corruption. Democrats are winning where they had been counted out for a generation, reshaping the American political map. Yet Trump remains president until 2028, and because Congress tends to stay less involved in foreign policy, he retains significant power. Presidents whose parties do poorly in midterms often become more active abroad, so analysts warn of possible erratic moves.
items.title: Republicans suffer historic midterm defeat; Trump's foreign policy risks rise

items.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said Wednesday that American voters rejected policies promoting hatred, sexism and climate change denial in Tuesday's elections. He posted the view on X, arguing the far-right wave is crumbling as it was in Brazil. Sanchez predicted a similar shift could soon occur ahead of Spain's Nov. 29 election.
items.title: Spanish Prime Minister Says US Voters Rejected Far-Right Policies Ahead of Spanish Elections

items.summary: The World Health Organization said six measures spanning public health, essential services and environmental protection could prevent an estimated 1. 6 million deaths annually while generating trillions in economic and fiscal benefits. In a report ahead of COP31 in Antalya, the agency estimated $3. 9 trillion in annual welfare gains plus $5. 4 trillion in fiscal gains. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said much climate-related harm is preventable with existing tools. The measures include heat warning systems, safe water and sanitation, cleaner household energy and fossil fuel pricing reform, which alone could avert 1. 2 million deaths yearly and avoid 16.
items.title: WHO: Six Health and Environmental Measures Could Save 1.6 Million Lives a Year

items.summary: RWE has secured contracts for three hydrogen-compatible gas-fired power stations in North Rhine-Westphalia, with a combined tender capacity of approximately 2,100 MW. The plants—730 MW at Voerde and two facilities of 700 MW each at Weisweiler and Werne—were awarded by the Federal Network Agency under the Electricity Supply Security and Capacity Act (StromVKG). They are intended to provide dispatchable electricity during periods when wind and solar generation fall short, with construction on the first station expected within weeks. RWE chief executive Markus Krebber said the plants would support supply security while using hydrogen-compatible technology.
items.title: RWE Wins Contracts for Three Hydrogen-Ready Gas Plants in Germany

items.summary: China's ambassador to Canada, Wang Di, said the China International Import Expo (CIIE) will boost trade ties between the two countries. He noted that this reflects Canada's strong interest in exploring the Chinese market and added that China's growing demand for high-quality products, combined with Canada's push for trade diversification, offers new opportunities for bilateral cooperation.
items.title: Chinese Ambassador Says CIIE Will Strengthen China-Canada Trade Ties

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed Madhya Pradesh Speaker to decide the anti-defection petition against Congress MLA Nirmala Sapre within two months, ruling that petitions under the Tenth Schedule must be decided expeditiously regardless of an assembly's remaining tenure. A bench with Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard a petition by Opposition leader Umang Singhar, who said proceedings had been pending since June 2024. Sapre denies the allegations, saying she resigned from Congress but did not join BJP. The court cited earlier judgments requiring time-bound decisions on such matters. Utkarsh Anand of Hindustan Times reported it.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Prompt Decision on Congress MLA's Anti-Defection Case

items.summary: Canva has laid off 1271 employees, about 22 per cent of its workforce. CEO Melanie Perkins said the decision followed what she called the company's hardest year in history. Affected staff will receive six months' salary plus extra benefits such as laptops, career coaching and a one-year LinkedIn Premium subscription. The company has not yet specified which regions are affected.
items.title: Canva Lays Off Over a Fifth of Its Workforce, Offering Generous Severance and Benefits

items.summary: The Delhi High Court stayed the dismissal of Jawaharlal Nehru University professor and Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, ruling that he had not been issued a notice before termination. The decision comes amid sexual misconduct allegations against him, an ongoing university inquiry, and political reactions. Akoijam has called his dismissal a political witch-hunt, alleging the BJP fabricated charges and that the university violated POSH law and confidentiality rules.
items.title: Delhi High Court Stays JNU Professor Dismissal Over Harassment Allegations

items.summary: A political dispute has erupted between the Aam Aadmi Party and the Bharatiya Janata Party over Delhi's air quality and stubble burning. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann rejected claims that farm fires cause Delhi's pollution, alleging accusations were made before harvest to defame Punjab. This follows Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa's claim that Punjab Police facilitated farm fires, which the AAP refuted. Separately, BJP held a day-long conclave and photo exhibition titled 'Wounds of 1984' in Chandigarh focusing on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, coinciding with Rahul Gandhi's visit to Punjab.
items.title: BJP and AAP clash over Delhi pollution as BJP holds 1984 conclave in Punjab

items.summary: Wang Xiaomei, a researcher at Zhejiang University's Research Center for Marxism Theory Innovation and Communication, argues that the Communist Party of China's Resolution on Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance extends beyond internal discipline to safeguard business development. She explains it translates constraints on officials into verifiable rules, lowering transaction costs and protecting property rights under China's Private Sector Promotion Law. The piece notes timely subsidy disbursement affects manufacturers' cash flow and that clean governance favors technology over connections. It concludes the resolution can help launch the 15th Five-Year Plan as of November 2, 2026.
items.title: How Party self-governance safeguards high-quality development

items.summary: A student at Bengaluru’s Mount Carmel, a deemed-to-be university, was barred from the remaining first-semester examinations after an invigilator noticed his unusually bulky spectacles on November 3. She monitored him for about 90 minutes before examining the glasses and reportedly hearing a sound when she tried them on. The authorities seized the device; the institution has not disclosed what he intended to do with it or whether he used it during the exam.
items.title: Bengaluru Institute Bars Student From Exams Over Smart Glasses

items.summary: Police shot dead Ghanakanta Gogoi, the prime accused in the October 26 Guwahati Hotel Bilas Inn attack that killed five people and injured a driver. Police said he was killed early Wednesday after allegedly attempting to flee custody while being taken for further investigation in Sivasagar district, nine days after the shooting. Victims' families called his death
items.title: Guwahati hotel shooting accused killed by police in escape attempt

items.summary: On Election Day, voters handed Democrats control of both houses of Congress in what editors describe as an overwhelming rebuke to President Donald Trump and Republicans. The Conversation’s senior politics editor Alfonso Serrano spoke with Charlie Hunt, a Boise State University scholar studying Congress and elections. They noted a broad Democratic shift across locations and counties, including substantial Hispanic vote shifts from 2024 of about 30-to-35 points in Texas and Florida. Democrats flipped Senate seats in five states and took the House. Editors attributed results to massive turnout, cross-party voting, and independent voter movement toward Democrats. Analysts also discussed campaign spending dynamics, noting diminishing returns on large Republican donations versus grassroots fundraising.
items.title: Democratic Blue Wave Sweeps Congress in Trump Rebuke

items.summary: President Donald Trump offered rare praise for Democrats after their midterm election victory, congratulating them in a FOX News interview while insisting the result was not a personal defeat. He refused to accept responsibility, instead blaming his own party's candidates and campaign efforts. Trump acknowledged that unpopular polls over the Iran war and rising oil prices contributed to Republican losses, though he defended his handling of the conflict. He signaled willingness to work with Democrats but threatened vetoes of their legislation. The White House warned voters could face "buyer's remorse" as gas prices fall.
items.title: Trump Praises Democrats After Midterm Loss, Blames Republicans and Iran War

items.summary: Supporters erupted in celebration as Talarico's projected victory was announced, potentially making him the first Democrat elected to the US Senate from Texas since 1988. The result remains unconfirmed and is described only as a projection. A supporter declared that 'up and down the ballot Texas is turning blue,' reflecting hopes for a broader Democratic shift in the state.
items.title: Talarico's Projected Texas Senate Win Sparks Democratic Jubilation

items.summary: Democrat Zack Mullock unseated Representative Jeff Van Drew, a leading opponent of offshore wind development, on Tuesday night in the race for New Jersey's second district. Mullock cited concerns about environmental and commercial fishing impacts while affirming support for renewable energy.
items.title: Offshore Wind Opponent Defeated in New Jersey Race

items.summary: Bloomberg, citing unnamed sources, reports India's coal, power and railway ministries are jointly working to triple the country's coal stockpile ahead of next summer. Current reserves stand at 18 million tons versus a target total of 55 million tons by March 31, when stocks hit their lowest since 2021. Railways raised carriage capacity for coal shipments last month by 20%, with another 7% increase demanded by March next year.
items.title: India Boosts Coal Stockpiles Amid Shortage Fears
